title: Twenty-Five Years After 'Dil Chahta Hai', Saif Ali Khan and Farhan Akhtar Are Reuniting — and It's a Thriller
excerpt: The young heartthrob and the debutant director who changed Hindi cinema in 2001 are reportedly teaming up for an intense moral thriller at Excel Entertainment.
body:
Twenty-five years ago, three boys drove a convertible down to Goa, fought over a girl, fell in and out of love, and accidentally rewrote what a Hindi film could sound like. One of those boys was **Saif Ali Khan**, playing the soft, lovelorn Sameer, and the man behind the camera, making his very first film, was a 27-year-old named **Farhan Akhtar**. **Dil Chahta Hai** didn't just turn its cast into stars. It changed the culture of how films get made in Bombay. Now, a quarter-century later, the two of them are circling each other again — and the industry is leaning in to listen.

According to a report in *Variety India*, Saif has signed on to headline an untitled thriller produced by Farhan Akhtar and Ritesh Sidhwani's **Excel Entertainment**. This isn't a sequel to anything, and it isn't nostalgia bait. The project is being described as an intense, edge-of-the-seat moral thriller — a story about ethics, difficult choices, and the kind of societal fault lines that don't resolve neatly. The film is still in the writing stage, the director hasn't been locked, and the leading lady opposite Saif is still being cast. Production is expected to begin by the end of 2026.


![Dil Chahta Hai — Photo: Wikimedia Commons](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/d/db/Dil_Chahta_Hai.jpg)


> "It was insane. I think it was the most fun because it was Goa, and we were very young. We shot on the beach and we partied as well." — Saif Ali Khan, recalling the Dil Chahta Hai shoot



> **"We shot on the beach and we partied as well." — Saif Ali Khan, recalling the Dil Chahta Hai shoot

What makes this reunion land harder than a routine casting note is the timing."**


What makes this reunion land harder than a routine casting note is the timing. *Dil Chahta Hai* completes 25 years this August, and Saif has spent the anniversary in a reflective mood, telling *Variety India* that Akhtar "was born to direct." He remembers a crew so disciplined — Zoya Akhtar was an assistant director on it — that they estimated a 105-day shoot from the script and wrapped on the 105th day. He remembers being asked to pick up litter on the beach so they'd leave it cleaner than they found it. "They changed the culture of how films are made," he said. To watch that partnership reconvene in 2026, with both men older, sharper and considerably more battle-scarred, is its own kind of full-circle satisfaction.


![Farhan Akhtar — Photo: Wikimedia Commons](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/1/13/FarhanAkhtar.jpg)


And Saif, frankly, has never been in better form to take on something this knotty. The man who once played the romantic pushover has spent the last few years building a second act out of menace and moral ambiguity — the villainous Vikram Aditya Singh in *Adipurush*, the cop in Netflix India's *Kartavya*. A morally compromised thriller protagonist is exactly the register where the new, weathered Saif is most magnetic. He's never coasted on charm alone the way some of his peers have, and a script built on ethics and consequence plays directly to his sharpest instincts.

The slate around him is stacked, too. Saif will next be seen in **Priyadarshan's Haiwaan** alongside **Akshay Kumar**, and he's attached to director Rahul Dholakia's historical Netflix film set around India's first General Election. The Excel thriller slots into an unusually meaty stretch of his career — less leading-man gloss, more character-actor weight, which is arguably the most interesting place a 50-something star can be.


![Ritesh Sidhwani — Photo: Wikimedia Commons](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/a/a4/Ritesh_Sidhwani_in_2016.jpg)


For the diaspora, the appeal is partly the nostalgia and partly the pedigree. *Dil Chahta Hai* was the film that travelled — it was a modest earner in rural India but a genuine phenomenon in the metros and overseas, the seventh-highest-grossing Hindi film abroad in its year. It spoke to a generation of urban, globally-minded Indians, many of whom became the NRIs now raising kids in Jersey City and Hounslow and Brampton. That audience has an almost cellular attachment to Akash, Sameer and Sid. A new Saif–Farhan collaboration, even an entirely unrelated thriller, taps a vein of affection that runs deep in living rooms from California to Surrey.

There are caveats worth keeping honest about. Nothing has been officially announced. No director, no co-star, no title, no shoot date beyond "end of the year." Excel has a habit of developing projects quietly and letting them simmer, and "in the writing stage" can mean anything from a polished draft to a one-line idea. This could be a film that arrives in 2028, or one that quietly dissolves. But the intent is real, and the symbolism is irresistible: the debutant director and the young heartthrob of 2001, now a powerhouse producer and a fearless character actor, choosing to walk back onto a set together.

If it happens, it won't be Goa, and they won't be young. But there's something to be said for two artists who helped each other grow up deciding, 25 years on, that they've still got unfinished business. We'll be watching for the first official word — and hoping the beach-cleaning discipline survived.
